With notifications enabled, you can see whether the KeepADB background service and Keep-Alive are running. If the connection drops, KeepADB lets you know right away. Wireless Debugging works fine without this permission too.
Android may restrict or stop Keep-Alive in the background unless KeepADB is exempt from battery optimization.
Keep-Alive can be restricted to known home or office Wi-Fi networks to block unauthorized debugging connections on foreign networks.

To recognize your trusted Wi-Fi (SSID/BSSID) when Keep-Alive starts in the background, KeepADB needs Location access set to “Allow all the time”. KeepADB never determines or stores your device’s position. On the next screen, open Permissions › Location and choose “Allow all the time” yourself; KeepADB cannot grant this for you. Without it, a network whose identity can’t be read is never trusted.
Background access: allowed. Allowed access points are recognized even when Keep-Alive starts in the background. KeepADB never reads or stores your device’s position.

Background access: restricted. If Keep-Alive starts in the background, Android may hide the Wi-Fi identity; KeepADB then treats the network as not allowed and doesn’t enable Wireless Debugging automatically until you open the app.
Background access: not needed in this setup. It is needed to check access points or Wi-Fi names while Keep-Alive runs in the background.
Location permission needed for trusted networks
Trusted-network mode needs Location access to identify your Wi-Fi network. Without it, Keep-Alive can’t confirm a trusted network and won’t re-enable automatically.
Prefer not to grant Location access? Trust all Wi-Fi networks instead — Keep-Alive will then re-enable on any connection.
Switched to \"trust all Wi-Fi networks\" mode.
Location access needed for Wi-Fi & access points
Location access is needed to identify the current Wi-Fi network and access points.
Sends the active Wireless Debugging endpoint (IP:port) via HTTP POST when enabled, and attempts a DELETE on shutoff (retried later if it fails).
Invalid URL. Must start with http:// or https:// with a valid host.
Please enter a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL before enabling sync.
This URL uses unencrypted HTTP — data is sent in plain text. Only use this on a trusted LAN or VPN.

Weaker check: a network name (SSID) is freely chosen and is no proof of an access point. Any access point broadcasting an allowed name is trusted, including one imitating yours. Mainly useful if you run several access points under one name.

Keep-Alive auto re-enable is paused: the current network\'s identity can\'t be determined. Check the location permission/service, or reopen the app if Keep-Alive started in the background. For a permanent fix, set Location to “Allow all the time”.
Android requires Location access before an app can read the current Wi-Fi network\'s name and ID. KeepADB uses this only to recognize trusted networks and never reads or stores your location.
Permission denied — staying on \"all Wi-Fi networks\" mode.
Couldn\'t determine the current network. Check that Wi-Fi is connected and Location permission is granted.

Keep-Alive auto re-enable is paused because the network\'s identity can\'t be read. This is usually a missing location permission or a disabled location service, but it can also happen after Keep-Alive started in the background; setting Location to “Allow all the time” fixes that permanently. Tap to fix it.
Current Wi-Fi network can\'t be identified (check Location permission).

Current network name can\'t be read, so it can\'t be added (check Location permission).
Tailscale may be disconnected, or was not auto-started after a reboot. Check Android\'s "Always-on VPN" setting for Tailscale.
System permission WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS missing. KeepADB cannot toggle Wireless Debugging until permission is granted.
Keeps the latest 128 redacted events on this device. Export opens the Android share sheet.
All saved networks, settings, and permissions will be deleted. The app will then close.
Shows the status notification in the drawer. Turning it off won’t affect Keep-Alive or widgets.
Required while Keep-Alive is active — Android needs it for the foreground service.

Shows the port and IP address in the persistent status notification, the USB host profile (name, IP, host), and the name and BSSID of new Wi-Fi networks in notifications. When on, these details may also be visible on the lock screen. When off, they are only shown in the app.
Keep display on while KeepADB is in the foreground
Keeps the screen on only while this app is open. The screen turns off normally as soon as you leave the app.
Show a separate notification while USB debugging is active. The host is selected manually.
Shows host profile status and actions in the USB-ADB notification. The profile name and endpoint details (IP, host) only appear when \"Show connection details in notifications\" is turned on.
Host profile selected — details in the app
Optionally offer or automatically enable Wifi-ADB from an active USB-ADB connection. Off by default; a manual OFF is never overridden.

Wireless Debugging opens an ADB port on your network. Use trusted private Wi-Fi or a VPN (e.g. Tailscale), and turn it off on public hotspots. Never share your endpoint publicly or accept an unexpected pairing prompt.
